sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: High-Precision Steel Injection Molding of Color Snap-Fit Plastic Kits

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (capital movement and establishment freedoms)
Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaties concluded with third states

Over 90 double taxation agreements in force, including US-Luxembourg, Germany-Luxembourg, France-Luxembourg, Belgium-Luxembourg, Netherlands-Luxembourg, China-Luxembourg, Japan-Luxembourg, Switzerland-Luxembourg, and UK-Luxembourg
EU-level free trade and investment protection agreements (CETA, EU-Japan EPA, EU-Singapore, EU-Vietnam)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (transposing AMLD4/AMLD5/AMLD6); Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 May 2019 on the RBE filings; Luxembourg Criminal Code Articles 506-1 to 506-8 (money laundering offence); Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended; Law of 12 July 2013 introducing the Societe en Commandite Speciale (SCSp); Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies, as amended; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (with restricted legitimate-interest access): the Luxembourg RBE is operated by Luxembourg Business Registers; following the CJEU rulings of 22 November 2022 (C-37/20 and C-601/20), public access to beneficial ownership entries is curtailed. Access is granted to the CSSF, the Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF), Luxembourg tax and customs authorities, notaries, banks, auditors, attorneys, and other obliged entities conducting client due diligence, and to any person able to demonstrate a legitimate interest via a reasoned request.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport or government-issued ID of each partner, UBO, and signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Consular office, foreign notary, or competent authority in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (HCCH 1961 Convention) where applicable; otherwise Consular Legalization through the Luxembourg Embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or official corporate extract for any corporate partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry or company registrar of the partner's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization, followed by sworn French/English translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming holding structure, source of funds, and corporate banking relationship
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature of the bank officer; Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization required where the issuing bank is outside the EU/EEA

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the Luxembourg law firm or authorised resident agent for incorporation formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction where the grantor is located

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO (utility bill, bank statement, or municipal certificate), not older than 3 months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, bank, or municipal authority of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sworn translation into French by a Luxembourg-registered translator; apostille not required for private utility bills but required for municipal and notarial certificates from non-EU states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory at onboarding and on an ongoing basis for all general partners, limited partners holding 25% or more, the partnership's signatories, and beneficial owners. Screening must cover the United Nations Consolidated List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (Regulation (EU) No 269/2014 and Common Position 2001/931/CFSP), Luxembourg national restrictive measures issued by the Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs, the OFAC SDN and Sectoral Sanctions Lists as a best-practice overlay for USD SWIFT wires and PayPal account usage, and a reputable PEP database covering foreign and domestic PEPs, immediate family members, and close associates. Any PEP or sanctions hit requires enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth evidence, and escalation to the Luxembourg AML compliance officer before incorporation proceeds. Payment rails are restricted to SWIFT wire and PayPal; each rail provider applies independent AML/CFT screening, and the Luxembourg SCSp must ensure that no sanctioned person is directly or indirectly connected.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via the lbr.lu platform and eJustice portal; RCSL — Registre de Commerce et des Societes de Luxembourg
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official filing language of the RCSL is French. The SCSp corporate name must be written in Latin (Roman) characters and must include the legal form indicator 'SCSp' or 'Societe en Commandite Speciale' in full. Names may be registered in French, German, or English, provided they are distinctive, not misleading, not contrary to public order or morality, and capable of French transliteration where necessary. For the ISIC 3240 scope, the name may reference action figures, collectible models, plastic model kits, or mecha hobby products, but must not create confusion with existing trademarks or registered Luxembourg entities.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque / Bank / Etablissement de credit (requires prior CSSF licence and Ministry of Finance authorisation)
Assurance / Insurance / Reassurance (requires prior Commissariat aux Assurances authorisation)
Societe de fiducie / Trust / Trustee / Fiduciary (requires Ministry of Justice authorisation)
Fonds d'investissement / SICAV / SICAF / FCP / AIF (requires prior CSSF authorisation as an investment vehicle)
Bourse / Stock Exchange / Clearing House (requires ministerial and CSSF approval)
Luxembourg / Etat du Luxembourg / Grand-Duche de Luxembourg (use restricted where it falsely implies state or public authority sponsorship)
Universite / Academie / Ecole nationale (requires Ministry of Education authorisation or regulatory approval)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The LBR name reservation is valid for 60 days and cannot be extended; if the incorporation deed is not filed before expiry, a new reservation request must be submitted. In case of rejection by the RCSL registrar, the applicant must first request written reasons stating the legal basis of the refusal. Within 30 days of the written refusal, an appeal may be lodged before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg, commercial chamber, through a Luxembourg-qualified avocat, using the accelerated petition procedure; the court may order the RCSL to register the name if it is found distinctive and compliant. A further appeal to the Cour d'appel de Luxembourg is possible within 40 days. Where rejection is based on a prohibited or sensitive token requiring prior ministerial consent, the applicant must obtain the respective authorisation from the competent ministry or supervisory authority before resubmission.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or domiciliation office is permissible for the SCSp provided it is supplied by a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation company and the address is declared to the RCSL as the registered office. Given the ISIC 3240 manufacturing scope, the SCSp will typically act as the investment and holding wrapper while the mechanical production, injection moulding, and packaging activities are carried out by an operational subsidiary with physical substance. Virtual office arrangements are therefore accepted at the Luxembourg holding level, but the partnership must retain access to its funds, records, and managerial oversight in Luxembourg. A purely artificial seat without any administrative substance may expose the SCSp to reassessment under the abuse-of-law doctrine and to non-cooperation findings in AML/CFT reviews.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (est. less than 5%) for a passive SCSp holding vehicle at the pre-incorporation stage. The RCSL does not perform routine unannounced physical inspections. However, the risk increases to 10-20% in the first 24 months if the partnership carries on substantive manufacturing activity or books Luxembourg VAT; unannounced inspections by the Administration des Contributions Directes, the Administration de l'Enregistrement et des Domaines, and CSSF AML/CFT inspectors can occur without warning in respect of registered offices, books, personnel files, and stock of the trading entity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, in particular Articles 27-28 (Société en Commandite Spéciale, 'SCSp'); Law of 31 May 1999 on the Luxembourg Business Registers ('LBR'); Law of 2 September 2011 on Access to Professions (establishment permit).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés de Luxembourg (RCSL), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); online filing via MyGuichet.lu / eRCSL portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Constitutive Partnership Agreement (Contrat de Société) with completed LBR registration application and published extract in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement for an SCSp; capital is freely set in the partnership agreement. No escrow account is prescribed by law. Contributions may be in cash or in kind, and must be fully subscribed and paid as specified in the contribution clause.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: At a meeting of the board of managers of [SCSp] duly convened, it was resolved: (1) that the subscription of partnership interests by the initial partners, as set out in the partnership agreement, is approved and ratified; (2) that the registered office of the partnership is established at [address] in Luxembourg, and the partnership is authorized to carry on the business of high-precision steel injection molding of color snap-fit plastic kits (ISIC 3240); (3) that [Name] is appointed as a manager with sole daily management powers, with authority to open bank accounts, execute filings, and obtain establishment and environmental permits; (4) that the manager is authorized to take all necessary steps for registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers and publication in RESA.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCSL via Luxembourg Business Registers / MyGuichet.lu online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request containing up to three proposed corporate names. The RCSL will verify that each proposal does not conflict with an existing registered name, does not infringe protected marks, and complies with Luxembourg rules on misleading trading names. Select the approved name before preparing the constitutive deed.
required_dossiers: Applicant and intended manager identification details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed name is rejected, an administrative appeal can be filed with the RCSL or an alternative approved name may be submitted immediately on the same portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Execution and Optional Notarization of the Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partners and, where desired, a Luxembourg notary; no notarial deed is mandatory for a private SCSp
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the SCSp constitutive partnership agreement (contrat de société) setting out the general and limited partners, contributions, profit-sharing ratios, management powers (gérant), registered office, purpose, duration and liquidation provisions. Execute the deed by all general and limited partners. If the partnership interests are offered to the public, the deed must be authenticated by a Luxembourg notary; if all interests are privately placed, a private deed is sufficient.
required_dossiers: Certified passport copies of all general and limited partners
Proof of residential address of each partner
Source of funds declaration for initial contributions
Curriculum vitae and criminal record extract of the proposed manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any defective clause in the signed agreement is cured by preparing an amending rider (avenant), signed by all partners and re-filed with the RCSL before registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing of the Constitutive Deed and Registration Application with the RCSL
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés via the Luxembourg Business Registers e-filing portal (MyGuichet.lu / eRCSL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the LBR e-filing portal, complete the standardized company registration questionnaire, attach the executed partnership agreement and the declaration of conformity if the deed is not notarial. Declare the beneficial owners in the LBR register, confirm the registered office, fill in the manager identification, and pay the registration fee. Submit electronically and monitor the case status.
required_dossiers: Proof of address of the Luxembourg registered office
Criminal record extract of the manager
Power of attorney if filing through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCSL issues a defect letter, the filer has fifteen calendar days to supply the missing information or to amend the filed instrument; a formal re-submission can be made after correction without losing the filing priority date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of RCS Registration Extract and Publication in RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCSL and Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the registration application is approved, the RCSL issues an official registration extract and assigns the Luxembourg matricule and RCS number. All constitutive deeds and declarations are automatically published electronically in RESA on the day following registration, giving third-party effect.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any discrepancy in the issued extract or RESA publication is cured by filing an application for correction with the RCSL through the same e-portal, accompanied by the supporting original deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Tax and Administrative Profile Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Use the official RCS extract to obtain a Luxembourg tax number and register for VAT with the AEDT by filing the standard VAT registration application. If the SCSp will hire employees, register as an employer with the CCSS without delay. Retain the RCS extract together with the tax and social security registrations for the eventual establishment permit application.
required_dossiers: Passive financial assets and activities questionnaire where relevant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax authority requests further information, respond in writing to the AEDT within one month; late VAT or social security registration is cured by filing retroactive with possible administrative fines and interest.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction Générale des Classes Moyennes (establishment permits); Administration de l'Environnement (environmental permits)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'Établissement (Establishment Permit) under the Law of 2 September 2011; Autorisation Environnementale (Environmental Operating Permit) for classified installations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Class 1 installation requiring a full environmental permit and, where thresholds in Annex II of the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 August 2009 are exceeded, a full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA); small-scale facilities may fall under the registration tier with no mandatory EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with the Luxembourg Water Management Law and Directive 2010/75/EU (Industrial Emissions Directive), including limit values for COD, BOD5, suspended solids and priority hazardous substances; VOC emissions must satisfy Directive 2004/42/EC and relevant BREF best available technique conclusions; generated plastic waste is subject to the Luxembourg Waste Management Act and the EU Waste Framework Directive 2008/98/EC.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Luxembourg Fire and Rescue Service (CGDIS) confirming compliance with the Grand-Ducal fire safety regulations; structural load inspection certificate from an approved engineering office; workplace safety approval from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering machinery, electrical safety and occupational health.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for income/corporate taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties; customs tariffs and export controls under Administration des douanes et accises. Primary e-government portal: MyGuichet.lu (guichet.lu); company registration through Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: An SCSp must first be registered with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) through a notary and an identified registered office, which generates a national business registration number (numéro d'immatriculation). For VAT, the SCSp or a non-resident taxable person carrying on taxable activities in Luxembourg must file a VAT registration application with the AEDT via MyGuichet.lu; the application requires: proof of RCS registration, statutes, identity documents of managers/partners, description of activities, and expected turnover. Non-resident entities without a permanent establishment may be required to appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative, subject to applicable treaties and administrative practice. The SCSp itself generally receives a Luxembourg VAT identification number if it performs an economic activity, without being subject to corporate income tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible; SCSp is fiscally transparent by default under Luxembourg income tax law, municipal business tax law, and net wealth tax law. Income, gains, and deductions flow through to its partners. The SCSp's registered office in Luxembourg creates a Luxembourg permanent establishment/fixed place of business only in appropriate circumstances; partners resident or with a permanent establishment in Luxembourg are taxed at the partner level. A non-resident partner with no Luxembourg permanent establishment is generally not subject to Luxembourg income tax on profits attributable to the transparent partnership, except where Luxembourg-source income categories apply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No direct check-the-box election exists under Luxembourg law; tax transparency of the SCSp is mandatory and not avoidable for income tax purposes. Available elections include: (i) VAT grouping election per Article 61 of the Luxembourg VAT Law to treat the SCSp with related entities as a single taxable person; (ii) option for the SCSp to become a taxable person for VAT if not already; (iii) application of EU ATAD hybrid mismatch rules (Law of 21 December 2018, as amended) may recharacterize a foreign transparent entity or partnership as opaque or transparent in cross-border situations; no unilateral domestic transparency election is available, but taxpayers may rely on the definitive classification drawn from the legal form and the place of effective management.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée – TVA), implementing the EU VAT Directive; administered by the AEDT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold for non-resident suppliers: any taxable economic activity performed in Luxembourg (including distance sales above the EU-wide €10,000 threshold in certain cases) requires VAT registration. Resident small enterprises may benefit from the small-business exemption only if annual turnover does not exceed EUR 35,000 (excluding VAT). Intra-EU acquisitions by taxable persons require registration above the annual acquisition threshold of EUR 10,000, unless opted into Luxembourg VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time national fiscal clearance or mandatory digital stamping is currently imposed on B2B or B2C e-invoices in Luxembourg. B2G e-invoicing is mandatory pursuant to Directive 2014/55/EU and must be transmitted through the Peppol network or an equivalent platform. For all invoices, the Luxembourg VAT law requires authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and legibility; this may be ensured by business controls, e-invoicing, EDI, or advanced electronic signatures. Invoices must be retained for 10 years. Luxembourg is monitoring the EU 'VAT in the Digital Age' (ViDA) initiative, which may introduce real-time digital reporting from 2027/2028.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods supplied by the SCSp and physically exported from Luxembourg/Europe to a destination outside the EU qualify for 0% VAT (export exemption) if dispatch or transport is carried out by the supplier or a third party on behalf of the supplier and is substantiated by export documentation. The supplier must obtain and preserve proof of export within the formalities set by Luxembourg customs and the AEDT, generally no later than 90 days from the supply. Services directly connected to exported goods and certain cross-border services (including manufacturing under customs supervision) may also be zero-rated if the recipient is established outside the EU and the services relate to goods that will be exported; all relevant contractual and documentary evidence must support the economic substance of the transaction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Luxembourg e-Douanes/ECS export notification, including the Movement Reference Number MRN)
Transport document evidencing physical exit from the EU (Bill of Lading, CMR consignment note, or air waybill)

Commercial invoice and payment/remittance evidence (bank SWIFT/MT103 confirmation or payment receipt; inward remittance certificate may be requested by the tax auditor as supplementary proof of consideration)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and Luxembourg customs audit export claims strictly. If the exporter cannot produce the required export proof within the legal deadline, the zero rating is denied and output VAT becomes payable at 17%, plus default interest of 0.6% per month (or the statutory rate in force) from the due date. A misdeclaration or fraudulent claim may result in a penalty tax of up to 100% of the tax evaded (10% for good-faith rectification, 25% for gross negligence, and up to 100% for intentional fraud), personal liability of managers, and criminal sanctions for customs fraud, including fines of up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment. Input VAT already claimed in relation to the export is clawed back if the zero-rating is disproved, and the assessment remains open under the standard Luxembourg statute of limitations (generally five years, which is extended in cases of fraud or failure to file).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); banking supervision and AML/CFT oversight of credit institutions coordinated with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) within the Eurosystem and the Single Supervisory Mechanism.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions in Luxembourg. There are no exchange controls, no prior-approval requirements, and no profit-repatriation restrictions for an SCSp. Non-resident partners may receive distributions through normal banking channels without BCL permit, subject only to AML/KYC documentation, sanctions screening, and any applicable withholding reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no mandatory reinvestment or escrow obligation for export receipts. An LU_SCSp may retain export proceeds in EUR or foreign currency in any bank account held with an authorised credit institution, and may freely convert, hedge, or disburse them, subject only to BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting thresholds where applicable.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / EUR Treasury Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium only for fintech and e-money institutions that hold a full Luxembourg CSSF/ECB e-money licence or a valid EU passport into Luxembourg under the Revised Payment Services Directive and E-Money Directive. Offshore digital EMIs without Luxembourg establishment, CSSF recognition, or a Luxembourg IBAN present Low viability for corporate treasury concentration because they cannot lawfully provide account-keeping in the SCSp's name, may lack safeguarding arrangements, and create disproportionate AML and operational risk. Such EMIs may be used only as ancillary collection channels, not as the primary clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The SCSp has no separate legal personality; account opening is therefore executed in the SCSp's name by its general partner or by an authorised natural-person representative. Luxembourg banks generally require an initial KYC interview; physical presence of the representative is the default for first-time onboarding, although CSSF-compliant video identification and remote opening are accepted by some Tier-1 banks on a risk-based basis. Where remote opening is allowed, notarised powers of attorney, original constitutional documents, and beneficial-owner declarations must be supplied before the account is activated.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex multi-tier ownership or nominee general partner creating ambiguity about ultimate beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Charted ownership tree, RBE beneficial-owner declaration, notarised deed of constitution, partnership agreement, general-partner resolution, certificate of incumbency for each intermediate entity, legal opinion from a Luxembourg counsel, passport copies of ultimate beneficial owners, and management-account records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large third-country capital injection or partner loan with undocumented source of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of source-account bank statements, source-of-wealth questionnaire, audited financial statements where available, personal and corporate tax filings, sale/purchase contracts, gift deeds, loan agreements with repayment schedules, bank references from remitting institutions, and a notarised source-of-funds certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Consumer toy and hobby-kit sector exposure to intellectual-property counterfeiting and unauthorised distribution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered trademark and design certificates, authorised agency or licence agreements, original purchase orders, manufacturing contracts, inspection certificates, quality assurance documents, distribution agreements, customs and EORI registration, and a written IP-compliance policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient Luxembourg economic substance for a pass-through SCSp conducting cross-border manufacturing trade.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg tax-residence certificate, substance file containing minutes of partner and general-partner meetings, registered-office details, management delegation agreements, bank account records, trade counterparty invoices, inventory and logistics documentation, payroll records, and transfer-pricing memorandum supporting arm's-length service fees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to or from high-risk jurisdictions, sanctioned entities, or problematic supply-chain intermediaries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening results, enhanced due-diligence questionnaire, export and import licences, end-user certificates, bills of lading or airway bills, customs declarations, harmonised-system classification notes, commercial invoices, and a board-approved sanctions and trade-compliance undertaking.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from partners should be remitted by SWIFT MT103 or TARGET2 in EUR with a unique end-to-end transaction reference (UETR), or by SEPA Credit Transfer when the remitter is within SEPA. The remittance information must specify 'EQUITY CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION – LU_SCSp – [partner legal name]' together with the SCSp's IBAN; for loans, 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN' and the loan-agreement reference must be provided. The receiving bank will verify the partnership agreement, capital-call notice, beneficial-owner declaration, AML/KYC acceptance, and the Luxembourg balance-of-payments purpose code for direct-investment equity or intercompany lending before crediting the capital escrow or operational account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 or MT202 with UETR for direct supplier payments and intercompany treasury transfers. For high-value imports of plastic pellets, steel components, and finished mecha model kits, a Commercial Letter of Credit issued on SWIFT MT700 provides settlement security, requiring documents such as the commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or airway bill, inspection certificate, and certificate of origin. EUR payments within the SEPA zone may be cleared via SEPA Credit Transfer; USD, CNY, or other non-EUR payments require correspondent banking lines, with CNH settlement available through offshore RMB clearing banks where applicable.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or non-convertible currencies in the Asia-Pacific supply chain
Deliverable USD/CNH forwards via offshore Chinese renminbi clearing banks

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation (RBE annual confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per calendar year; must be carried out within 12 months of the previous confirmation, generally triggered by the RBE annual reminder
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 1,250 for natural persons and up to EUR 25,000 for legal persons per violation; court-ordered coercive penalty (astreinte) may be imposed; repeated non-compliance can lead to public prosecution and administrative strike-off from the Luxembourg Business Registers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) filing with the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end if the SCSp exceeds the small undertaking thresholds (e.g., 31 July for a calendar-year entity); no filing required if the SCSp qualifies as small and is not otherwise subject to a statutory audit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 10,000 for late or non-filing; court order with daily penalty payment (astreinte) for continued default; persistent failure may result in administrative strike-off from the RCS and loss of substantive rights to enforce partnership claims.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit is triggered if the SCSp exceeds two of the three following annual thresholds: total balance sheet above EUR 4.4 million, net turnover above EUR 8.8 million, or average workforce above 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory if required by the partnership agreement or by the RCS in specific circumstances.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP pursuant to the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies; IFRS may apply if the SCSp becomes part of consolidated financial statements or voluntarily opts for IFRS where legally permitted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Law of 13 January 2019, the SCSp must keep its beneficial ownership data accurate and must file a confirmation at least once per year. Any transfer of partnership interests that changes beneficial ownership must be reported to the RBE within 30 days of the event.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Decisions of Partners (Registre des décisions des associés)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined effective rate for Luxembourg City (CIT 17.00% + solidarity surcharge 7.00% of CIT + municipal business tax 6.75%). The SCSp is fiscally transparent by default, so this rate is allocated and applied at the level of each partner on its profit share.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp fiscal transparency: no CIT or municipal business tax at the fund level. Participation exemption: 100% exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains on ≥10% participations held ≥12 months. IP box regime: 80% exempt income on qualifying IP => effective ~5.2% CIT on IP royalties. R&D tax credit of up to 30% of eligible R&D payroll and expenses (cap EUR 150,000 per annum); investment tax credits of 8% to 12% for qualifying equipment. Municipal business tax applies only if a Luxembourg permanent establishment exists. Tax loss carryforward limited to 5 years for transparent partnership losses allocated to non-resident partners absent a Luxembourg PE; no carryback.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 300 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed through the professional e-filing portal eCDF of the Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) via MyGuichet.lu; VAT returns are separately e-filed via the eTVA portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Paper filing: 30 June of the year following the fiscal year-end. Electronic filing: automatic extension to 31 December of the same year. The SCSp, being fiscally transparent, generally does not file Form 300 unless it has made an elective opaque classification or carries on a taxable Luxembourg PE; non-resident partners report their allocable profit share in their own jurisdictions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the SCSp, registered office in Luxembourg, RCS number, legal form code, principal activity (ISIC 3240 – manufacture of games and toys; high-precision plastic injection molding of action figure kits).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter RCS extract and list of partners as an annex. Non-resident partners are not identified as Luxembourg taxpayers unless they carry on business through a Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare the closing date of the commercial accounting year (normally 31 December) and confirm that the taxable period does not exceed 12 months.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that the partnership accounts and the partners' local tax year are aligned; a Luxembourg tax year other than the calendar year requires an ACD approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net income per Luxembourg GAAP, including adjustment items such as non-deductible representation expenses (50% limitation), non-deductible taxes, and excessive remuneration of partners; the result is then allocated to partners according to the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SCSp elects transparent treatment and has no Luxembourg PE, enter zero taxable income and attach the allocation schedule; each partner's share is reported by the partner in its residence state.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: State prior-year losses utilised in the current period and the remaining balance; attach a loss schedule reconciled with the statutory 5-year carryforward window and the change-of-ownership restrictions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No Luxembourg loss attribute is granted to a non-resident partner unless that partner holds a Luxembourg PE connected to the loss-making activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 17% CIT rate, 7% solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax rate to the taxable base after allocation; compute available credits (R&D credit, investment credit, IP box exemption).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the box only where the SCSp is subject to Luxembourg tax due to a PE or opaque election; otherwise the box is not applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Attachment detailing related-party transactions: intercompany royalties, cost-plus manufacturing margins, shared marketing costs and intercompany loans with arm's-length interest.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident manufacturing partners must obtain a Luxembourg TP documentation set if the group turnover threshold is met; the master file is retained in Luxembourg at the registered office.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: astreinte (Zwangsgeld) up to EUR 25,000 under Article 178 AO; automatic 10% tax surcharge on assessment plus monthly delay interest of 0.6% of the unpaid amount under LIR Article 155; deliberate omission or false declaration constitutes tax fraud punishable by imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years and/or a criminal fine of up to EUR 250,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15.00% general Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends (LIR Article 147). A default transparent SCSp is not subject to dividend WHT on distributions to partners because the partnership is not a taxpayer; however, an SCSp that has elected non-transparent treatment may trigger the 15% WHT, reduced to 0% where the parent-subsidiary directive applies (≥10% holding, 12-month minimum holding) or under the participation exemption conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To benefit from DTA relief on distributions recharacterised as taxable dividends, the non-resident partner must submit to the ACD: (1) a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by its home tax authority, dated within 12 months and apostilled or legalised as required; (2) the relief application form (ACD form 26/27) filed at the payer's tax office before the distribution or as a refund claim; (3) beneficial ownership evidence, including substance documentation if the partner is located in a low-tax jurisdiction; (4) the parent-subsidiary directive form where applicable. The SCSp agreement and partner register must evidence the profit share ratio and the 12-month holding intent.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% statutory WHT for payments made after 1 January 2019 (the former 15% royalty WHT under LIR Article 146 was repealed); treaty rates on royalties are therefore irrelevant in practice. Interest: 0% statutory WHT on arm's-length commercial debt interest; interest on profit-participating loans is recharacterised as a dividend and taxed at 15%, subject to treaty reduction (commonly 10%–15% under Luxembourg DTAs); payments must be supported by a written loan agreement, commercial rationale and complete substance to avoid anti-abuse recharacterisation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File and Local File become mandatory when the worldwide consolidated group turnover reaches EUR 50,000,000; for smaller SCSp structures, the ACD may still request contemporaneous documentation for intercompany transactions exceeding EUR 100,000 per category (ACD Circular L.I.R. No. 56/1-56bis/1, OECD TP Guidelines).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not have UAE-style sectoral ESR, but the economic substance doctrine is enforced through general anti-abuse rules: Article 6 of the Tax Adjustment Act (abuse of forms), ATAD-implemented anti-hybrid and exit rules, and the substance circulars governing intragroup financing and IP holding companies. A SCSp deriving royalties from the anime figure IP or holding substantial cash must demonstrate real presence in Luxembourg: local strategic decision-making, a Luxembourg-resident manager, office premises, board/partner meetings, and actual business activity; absence of substance causes the ACD to disregard the SCSp, deny treaty and participation exemption benefits, and restate income to the beneficial owner.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of sales income from PayPal and SWIFT wire channels, overstatement of deductible intercompany royalties paid to a foreign related manufacturer, or submission of a knowingly false Form 300 declaration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fraud penalties under the General Tax Law (AO): imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years and/or a criminal fine of up to EUR 250,000; civil reassessment with 10% late-payment surcharge and 0.6% monthly delay interest; publication of the conviction and disgorgement of assets traced to the evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax debt and civil restitution where they committed a faute grave or fraud (Company Law Article 495, Civil Code Article 1382); criminal courts may impose travel bans, freezing of personal bank accounts, and confiscation orders; imprisonment applies to the individual who signed the false return.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / Abuse of SCSp transparency
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SCSp as a letterbox to channel toy manufacturing royalties and avoid dividend withholding tax, while all management and economic activity occurs offshore; or registering an SCSp with no Luxembourg decisions, no local payroll, and no office, merely to obtain tax treaty access.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ACD requalification of the SCSp as an opaque corporation under the GAAR, reassessment with the 15% dividend WHT plus 0.6% monthly interest and 10% penalty, and denial of DTA benefits; administrative fines up to EUR 25,000 for failure to provide substance information; potential strike-off of the entity from the RCS.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors risk joint liability for all unpaid taxes through the faute de gestion doctrine, personal civil restitution of distributions made without substance, administrative travel bans during the tax fraud investigation, and disqualification from management for up to 10 years upon conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the Luxembourg register of beneficial owners (RBE) declaration within 30 days of incorporation or after a partner change; failure to identify and verify the UBO of the SCSp, or failure to maintain customer due-diligence files for PayPal and wire-transfer counterparties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines from EUR 5,000 to EUR 1,250,000 under the amended law of 12 November 2004; criminal penalties up to EUR 1,000,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for wilful breaches; the RCS may suspend the partner voting rights and the ACD may freeze the SCSp bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers who knowingly omit UBO disclosure incur personal liability for the AML fine, personal disqualification orders, travel bans in the context of the financial intelligence investigation, and imprisonment for deliberate laundering of undeclared route payments.
